summary: Henry Sullivan Jarrett worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He succeeded Heinrich Blochmann and served as Member and Secretary at the Board of Examiners in Calcutta from circa 1870 to 1894.

Henry Thomas Colebrooke was an Indologist who studied under Citrapati. He served in the Bengal Civil Service, East India Company, Fort William College, and Supreme Council of Bengal, and later directed the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland.

Herbert Franke studied at Cologne, Bonn, and Berlin under Erich Haenisch, working in sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history. He served as president of the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities and professor at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich.

Herbert Härtel, who studied under Ernst Waldschmidt, was a scholar of Indology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He directed the Museum für Asiatische Kunst from circa 1963 to 1986 and held a professorship at Humboldt University of Berlin.
Herbert Niel Randle was an Indologist and philosopher. He served as Librarian at the India Office from circa 1933 to 1949 and was attested as Librarian at the India Office Library in 1973.

Herbert V. Guenther worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Saskatchewan and under teachers including Damcho Rinchen, Geshe Ngawang Nyima, and Tarthang Tulku, later serving as professor at Saskatchewan from circa 1964 to 1984.

Herbert Weir Smyth studied at Swarthmore, Harvard, Leipzig, and Göttingen, working in linguistics. He held academic posts at Williams College, Johns Hopkins University, Bryn Mawr College, and Harvard University (~1901–1925).
Herman Kellgren was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Eugène Burnouf, Philippe-Édouard Foucaux, and Hermann Brockhaus. He held a post at the University of Helsinki from circa 1849 to 1856.
Hermann Beckh was a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin from circa 1903 to 1907 and held a post there from circa 1908 to 1921.
Hermann Beythan was a scholar in Indology and linguistics who studied under the traditional teachers Ramasami Aiyar and Radscha Pillai.

Hermann Brockhaus studied at Leipzig University and under August Wilhelm Schlegel, working in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He held professorships at the University of Jena and Leipzig University, and co-founded the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft.

Hermann Brunnhofer was an Indologist who studied under Albrecht Weber. He succeeded Franz Kielhorn and held posts at Goldingen Gymnasium and the University of Bern, where he served as Titularprofessor from 1901 to 1914.
Hermann Camillo Kellner was an Indologist who studied under Hermann Brockhaus from circa 1866 to 1870. He served as a Gymnasialprofessor at the Gymnasium zu Zwickau from circa 1872 to 1904.

Hermann Collitz was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Göttingen under Theodor Benfey. He served as professor at Bryn Mawr College (1885–1907) and later as professor of Germanic philology at Johns Hopkins University.

Hermann Goetz studied at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich and worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He served as curator at Baroda Museum and Picture Gallery (~1939–1953) and held a post at Heidelberg University (~1961–1976).

Hermann Grassmann studied at Frederick William University Berlin, specializing in Indology and linguistics. He taught at the Gewerbeschule and Friedrich-Wilhelms-Gymnasium, and served as professor at the Marienstiftsgymnasium Stettin from 1852 to 1877.

Hermann Hirt was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Freiburg and Leipzig University. He held academic posts at Leipzig University from circa 1896 to 1912 and at the University of Giessen from circa 1912 to 1935.

Hermann Jacobi studied at Bonn, Berlin, and Calcutta, working in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He held posts at the universities of Münster and Kiel, as well as Munich, Cologne, and Bonn, where he was attested as professor in 1925.

Hermann Kulke, an Indologist and historian, completed his PhD at the University of Freiburg. He was appointed Chair of Asian History at the University of Kiel in 1988 and held an attested post at Heidelberg University in 2004.

Hermann Oldenberg studied at Humboldt University of Berlin, working in Indology and Buddhist studies. He held professorships at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1881–1889), the University of Kiel (~1889–1904), and the University of Göttingen (~1904–1920).
